identification: Optical-micrometer transit theodolite, almost certainly an E.R. Watts & Son (London) Microptic No.1 type, c1935-1950: black crackle/enamel finish, enclosed glass circles, large vertical-circle housing with hinged illuminating mirror on top, silver micrometer drum on the standard, plate bubble, three-screw tribrach base (with white residue/paint on the tribrach). In a worn black-painted wooden carry box with leather straps. No tripod. Catalogue calls it a 'surveyors level'; it is a theodolite, not a level. Armitage estimate A$40-80.

viewing_check: Read maker plate and serial on the standard or base (E.R. Watts & Son London, Microptic No.1, serial); look through the eyepiece and the reading microscope for clear optics and visible circle graduations (fungus/haze kills value); check circles and clamps turn, mirror flap intact; what the white residue on the tribrach is; box interior fittings and any accessories (eyepiece, plumb bob, tools).
